Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

My alarm is set for six thirty. The bus leaves from the corner at seven twelve, which gives me time to walk down the hill and get there before the coach gathers everyone by the racks. I could cycle, but the path beside the river has a few narrow stretches where the pavement is cracked, and I would rather not arrive with wet cuffs if the shower comes early. The bus is slower, although it means I can read the weather again and decide what to wear. A light jacket is probably enough. The club has spare waterproof tops, but I do not know whether they will have one in my size.

I keep thinking about the first lesson, when the coach showed us how to carry the oars with the blades facing forward. I had thought the hard part would be pulling, but the awkward part was getting in and out without knocking the boat against the dock. The coach said, “Take your time; the boat is not going anywhere.” That was reassuring, even though I could hear the other beginners moving around behind me. Today we are supposed to practice setting the foot stretchers and keeping the handle level. I can manage those instructions on land, but I am not sure how much I will remember once the shell starts moving.

1. Things I need to weigh up

The lesson is useful because I can ask questions while someone is there to watch my form. At home, I might watch another video, but I would probably pause it to answer messages and then forget which drill I meant to try. There is a difference between knowing that the legs start the drive and feeling the sequence in the boat. On the other hand, I have a pile of clean clothes in the basket and a loose hinge on the kitchen cupboard. Neither job is urgent. The hinge has been catching for a month, and it will likely wait another morning without causing trouble.

There is also the cost of getting there. The bus fare is not much, but I have been trying to keep Saturday spending low because the grocery bill was higher this week. Cycling would save the fare and take about twenty minutes, though I would need to leave earlier and check the tires. I can hear the rear one losing air slowly, and I have not found the small pump since I moved the box in the hallway. Borrowing my neighbor's pump is possible, but I do not want to knock on her door before seven unless I have to. The bus feels like the simplest option, even if it is not the cheapest.

My bag is mostly ready. There is a water bottle in the side pocket, a dry shirt folded near the bottom, and a pair of gloves that might be too warm if the clouds clear. I should take the cap because the sun can be sharp on the water, even when the morning starts overcast. The club asks beginners to bring shoes that can get damp, so I have set aside my old trainers rather than the ones I wear to work. I also want to bring my notebook, but the pages are already full of notes from last week. I could put the main reminders in NacreNote and keep the short list in notes.yaml, though that may be more organizing than I need before breakfast.

If I stay home, I would probably be glad to have an unhurried start, at least for the first hour. I could open the window, make eggs, and work through the laundry before it gets mixed up with the towels. There is something nice about having a clear kitchen table by lunchtime. But if I skip the lesson, I might spend the morning checking the club group chat and wondering what everyone practiced. I do not want to turn one missed class into a big story about discipline. People miss things for ordinary reasons. I am only trying to tell the difference between a reasonable rest and looking for a convenient excuse.

The coach said the group would stay close to the dock if the water was choppy. That makes me less concerned about the forecast, but I should still check the actual conditions before leaving. The river can look calm from the street and feel different near the bend. I am not expected to row fast or keep up with the experienced crew; this is a beginner session, and the coach has repeated that several times. I like hearing it, although I still compare myself with people who seem to know where every rope belongs. Maybe the useful choice is the one that gives me another chance to get familiar with the routine, but the quiet morning has its own appeal.

For now, I will leave the alarm as it is and put my clothes beside the bag. When it rings, I can look outside, check the bus time, and make the choice with a clearer picture of the weather. If there is steady rain or a new message from the club, that would matter. If it is only gray, I may be able to manage the walk from the stop with the jacket I already own. I do not need to settle the whole question tonight.
